# Real TLS handshakes, captured by scripts/capture_transcripts.py.
#
# Both sides are Python's ssl in memory-BIO mode, pumped by hand - no
# sockets - so this is every byte that crossed between two implementations
# that are not ours. It is the fixture the record layer and the handshake
# state machine are developed against before any live connection, because a
# state machine bug is the category unit tests are worst at catching.
#
# One record per line: "<field> <transcript> <value>". The bytes change on
# every capture (fresh randoms and keys), so a diff against the old file is
# noise; what matters is that the suites listed are the ones we want.

version tls12_rsa_aes128_sha TLSv1.2
cipher tls12_rsa_aes128_sha AES128-SHA
to_server tls12_rsa_aes128_sha 
to_client tls12_rsa_aes128_sha 
secret tls12_rsa_aes128_sha RSA 7f05fc7b3d6f459b 03035775af99a04983e71b031482612ad6d9e00ba865500a9576a8710024445e8542fe74a2093794173b8cff28838bbc
secret tls12_rsa_aes128_sha CLIENT_RANDOM 6e0c84bcad4b7f5fc279aac4796f7f1b43e79685b26901c1805a360818cfd124 b9579429c0c0509460f2171a38763ee6a9c4ec8322693f4c5582c855738523af68c7117d5edeedfaf82ba80268b4b3ee

to_server tls12_ecdhe_aes256_sha384 
to_client tls12_ecdhe_aes256_sha384 
secret tls12_ecdhe_aes256_sha384 CLIENT_RANDOM 7d2625fc44ea955a9f52e2e296df3f039405b59fd00dd49f2ced62157bf3d3b0 a66e466e43c3dde84f8c9ab52883a71cb75134d3053c4e48c9496b7a740418d556746c043db7f433ee1d71b9683d0a2b
